title: Latin music in Japan
summary: Japanese radio played Latin music around the clock, loved Los Panchos, Perez Prado and Cugat, and stocked his Tico records.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, okay. Ahh did they have any Latin music recordings there?
Oh yes, Los Panchos, Los Panchos was ....
Oh!! They was crazy about them.
Okay. What about on the radio? Did they ever play Latin music?
They was playing twenty-four hours, Latin music.
Like for instance, Perez Prado was a big name up there. Ahh Cugat, it was a big name too, and then us after Tito Puente. He went up there, but we come back here ....
.... the same year and that. So then, would you say the Japanese people liked Latin-American music?
What about in record stores, were there Latin-American records?
What about your stuff, was it there in records racks?
Yes, before we got there they had records that we recorded maybe five or six years.
